Cross country is a rugged business and it demands every quality, both physical and mental, and it has yet to be proved that it upsets track runners, particularly if they train like Pirie.
John Bromley went off with the lead over the long 7th stage, but with Pirie and Olney running stride for stride, they soon overhauled him and went well away into the lead.
Charlie Smart who at the age of 44 is running better than ever set off with the Belgrave baton with Gordon Pirie of S.L.H. some 15 seconds behind.
The outstanding race of the day was no doubt the 880 yds in which Bob Taylor came up against Gordon Pirie who he had recently defeated over the same distance.

Pirie, Norris and Foord fought it out all the way and our chaps were never in the hunt for the leading positions. Our leading runner just managed to beat South London's 6th, but by some remarkable packing, six men in 14 places and 64 seconds, we gained second place in the team race.

There is nothing unusual about the training of Iharos, Chataway, Zatopek, Pirie, Norris Hewson and the rest - these men are quite normal individuals - everyone can adopt the same technique but the work involved must be built up over a number of years.

In the junior race we saw a new Pirie, for the manner in which North slammed the field in such conditions, was a revelation. It seems almost a travesty of justice that he was not awarded his international vest.

What is it about men like Firth, Driver, Pirie and company which enables them always to strike the front within half a mile or so? Pat Newell, running in his first cross country race this season, clung tenaciously to a good start and was always placed around the forty mark.

In no way deterred by the reputations enjoyed by his opponents, Charlie Dabbs clung to the redoubtable Pirie and title-holder Ernie Earl sufficiently well to gain a notable 3rd place in the 3 miles, clocking 14:21.8---a personal best.
Pirie was an easy winner for S.L.H. smashing previous course records set by Hyman and Foord by nearly a minute. Ken Miller was a good third, with Thresher 7th, Walker 8th and Shippen 10th.
For besides the oppresive heat he also had to contend with Messrs. Pirie, Hyman, Eldon & Co. Pat ran, relatively, as well as anybody in the field to record 14:14, but was outside the first six.
Perhaps the County needs a Pirie or Hewson to bring back the crowds. If so, there is plenty of potential amongst the County's Youth, and Belgrave have their fair share of it.

Gordon Pirie crosses the line in the Surrey Road Relay Championship of 9th September 1961, taking South London Harriers to victory. Gordon's time was a full two minutes faster than any one else on that day.
